derivedFrom.corpus: A private reference set of past-paper-style material supplied by the site operator: practice and mock papers, preparation guides, formula sheets and syllabus analyses.
derivedFrom.policy: The corpus is input only. It is gitignored, never copied into content/ or public/, never quoted in the UI, the README, solutions or commit messages. Only the aggregate numbers on this page are carried forward.

paperFormat.negativeMarkingNote: No source states a penalty for wrong answers and no reference paper shows one. The app scores +1 per correct answer and 0 otherwise, and tells the user to answer every question.
paperFormat.medium: Computer-based multiple choice, one correct option

officialBands.source: src-analysis — both syllabus-analysis documents state a 40%-30%-30% easy/medium/complex structure, and give the split module by module.

practicePaperSignal.note: Practice material in the reference set labels every item with a p-value (proportion answering correctly). Only three values appear, 0.94, 0.85 and 0.65, one per official band.

mapping.label: Recall
mapping.description: One definition, one formula, or a direct reading. No intermediate step.

mapping.label: Single step
mapping.description: Substitute the given values into one formula.

mapping.label: Standard
mapping.description: Two steps, or one step plus a rearrangement or unit conversion.

mapping.label: Multi-step
mapping.description: Three or more steps, or combining two different results.

mapping.label: Challenging
mapping.description: Non-obvious setup, a case split, or a general rather than numeric answer.

paperBlueprint.note: How one 48-question paper is built. The mock-exam mode follows this exactly, so a mock has the same shape as the real thing even though the bank behind it is deeper and more evenly spread.

bankTargets.note: How many questions to author per subtopic. Deliberately flatter than the paper blueprint: a practice bank needs enough depth in every subtopic to be worth revising from, with a floor of three so no corner of the syllabus is a dead end. The blueprint above, not this table, decides what a mock paper looks like.

stemLength.note: Mathematics stems are terse and often symbol-only. Physics stems set up a short scenario, then ask for one quantity.

conventions.language: English throughout. Short sentences, no idioms, no culture-specific scenarios. Written to be read by a non-native speaker under time pressure.
conventions.optionStyle: Four options labelled A-D. Options are the same kind of object as each other — all numbers with the same unit, or all intervals, or all equations. Never 'all of the above' or 'none of the above'.
conventions.optionOrdering: Numeric options are listed in ascending order where that does not give the answer away; otherwise the correct index is spread evenly across A-D.
conventions.correctIndexBalance: Across the bank, each of A/B/C/D holds the correct answer 20-30% of the time.

mathNotation.delimiters: LaTeX inside $...$ for inline and $$...$$ for display
mathNotation.intervals: (-\infty, 3] \cup [5, +\infty) — round brackets for open, square for closed
mathNotation.fractions: \dfrac in options so they render at full size
mathNotation.angles: Degrees with ^\circ for values (\sin 120^\circ); radians with \pi for periods and intervals
mathNotation.sequences: a_n, S_n, common difference d, common ratio q — the corpus uses q, not r

physicsNotation.units: SI, upright, with a thin space before the unit: 12.5\ \mathrm{m/s}
physicsNotation.gravityNote: The build brief asked for g = 9.8 m/s^2. Every paper and formula sheet in the corpus uses g = 10 m/s^2, so the bank uses 10 to match what candidates will actually see. The value is written into the stem of every question where it matters, so nothing depends on the reader guessing.
physicsNotation.significantFigures: Answers come out to 1-3 significant figures. Numbers in stems are chosen so the arithmetic is doable in about 75 seconds without a calculator.

math.name: Evaluate a set operation on two described sets
Decide whether one condition is necessary, sufficient, or both, for another
Give the solution set of a quadratic or rational inequality as an interval
Apply AM-GM to find a minimum
State the domain of a function built from a root, a log and a denominator
Pick the odd / even / monotonic function from four candidates
Find the inverse of a simple invertible function
Evaluate or compare logarithmic and exponential expressions
Evaluate a trigonometric value at a special or reduced angle
Apply a double- or half-angle identity given one ratio and a quadrant
State the period, range or monotonic interval of a transformed trig function
Solve a triangle with the sine or cosine rule, or find its area
Find a missing term or sum of an arithmetic or geometric sequence
Recover the general term from S_n, or S_n from a recurrence
Differentiate and evaluate, or find a tangent line
Use the sign of the derivative to find a monotonic interval or an extremum
Find the slope, inclination or equation of a line through given points
Test two lines for parallel or perpendicular, or find their intersection
Write or read off the equation of a circle
Recover a conic's equation from focus, axis, eccentricity or focal length
Express one vector in terms of two others in a named figure
Use the dot product to find an angle, a magnitude, or test perpendicularity
Solve a linear equation in a complex unknown, or find a modulus
Find an angle, a length or an area in a triangle, circle or polygon
Count arrangements or selections with permutations and combinations
Compute a classical probability from a described experiment
Combine events: exclusive, complementary, independent, or conditional
Compute mean, median, variance or standard deviation of a data set
Read a probability off a binomial or normal distribution

Apply v = v0 + at or s = v0 t + at^2/2 to a body starting from rest
Distinguish average velocity from average speed on a curved path
Free fall: time, speed or height, with g stated in the stem
Hooke's law, sometimes with two loadings to recover the natural length
Decide whether an object slides, and find the friction force
Find the range or an extreme value of a resultant of two or three forces
Newton's second law on a horizontal surface or a smooth incline
Compute work done by a named force over a stated displacement
Apply the work-energy theorem to find a final speed
Change in gravitational or elastic potential energy, with sign
Impulse of a named force over a stated time
Conservation of momentum in a one-dimensional collision
Projectile motion: time of flight, range, or a component of velocity
Relate v, omega, T and R, including belt- and axle-linked points
Orbital speed or period from universal gravitation
Which quantity is maximal at the equilibrium or the extreme point of SHM
Period, frequency, wavelength or wave speed
Charge sharing between identical spheres, or Coulomb's law
Field strength from a point charge, or the field at the midpoint of a pair
Potential difference from the work done moving a charge
Series and parallel resistance, current split, or power dissipated
Separate heating loss from total power in a motor or a source with internal resistance
F = BIL, or the Lorentz force and the radius of a charged particle's path
Faraday's law with N turns and a stated flux change
Lenz's law: the direction of an induced current
Gas law at constant volume, pressure or temperature, with Celsius to Kelvin
First law of thermodynamics: sign bookkeeping for Q, W and internal energy
Reflection, refractive index, critical angle or total internal reflection
Thin lens formula and magnification
Conditions for interference or diffraction to be observable
Photon energy, work function and maximum kinetic energy
Energy-level transition and the wavelength of the photon emitted
Balance a nuclear decay equation, or find a mass defect and binding energy

outOfScope.note: Named in no source and absent from the reference corpus. Kept out of the bank so practice time is not wasted.

originalityPolicy.rule: Every published item is original work modelled on the profile above. Same skill tested, different scenario, different quantities, different wording.
originalityPolicy.shingleRule: Flag any stem or solution sharing a run of 8 or more consecutive normalised words with any reference item. Numbers are folded to a placeholder first, so swapping the quantities does not evade the check.
originalityPolicy.numericRule: Flag any stem reusing a reference item's ordered numeric run of 3 or more values when the surrounding wording is also more than 45% similar.
originalityPolicy.onFlag: Rewrite. Never ship a flagged item.
